To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT FOR REVIEW — Stop using Brightline Pro 6% batch LX2291

Please check your developer before your next colour client. This is a safety issue, not just an inconvenience.

Kelvin Trade has confirmed a filling error affecting Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L, batch LX2291. Some bottles in this batch may contain 12% (40 vol) instead. You cannot rely on the 6% label.

STOP USING BATCH LX2291 STRAIGHT AWAY.

WHIT TO CHECK

Check the batch code on the BASE OF THE BOTTLE. It is not on the box, so checking the outer carton isnae enough. Check every bottle individually, including:
- Open bottles sitting in your trolley.
- Bottles already out at your station.
- Unopened stock in the back.

Kelvin says this batch was supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026. I bought mine from the rep on 28 October. Check the actual code rather than going by when you think you bought it. If the code is missing or unreadable, put the bottle aside and ask Kelvin to confirm before using it.

Separate affected bottles from usable stock and clearly mark them “DO NOT USE — LX2291”. Dinnae try a test service or dilute it down yourself. Kelvin says other batches and other strengths are not affected.

WHAT HAS HAPPENED HERE

On Saturday, I used a new bottle labelled 6%, batch LX2291, for a bleach retouch. The lift was much faster than usual, and the client reported burning at the crown after 18 minutes. I stopped and rinsed immediately. There was redness at the crown and nape. No client details are being shared here.

Another renter has also confirmed LX2291 after unusually fast lift and very hot foils on Thursday. She initially thought the heater was too close. There was no reported burn in that case, but the colour came out brassy and patchy.

Developer stronger than intended can make lightening faster and harder to control, with more heat, scalp irritation or chemical burns. It can also leave hair overprocessed, dry, fragile or breaking, and give uneven results. These signs do not prove what strength is in a bottle: check the batch. A normal patch test does not make a mislabelled developer safe.

IF SOMEONE REACTS IN THE CHAIR

Stop the service immediately. Dinnae dismiss burning or unusual heat as normal tingling, and do not wait for the colour to finish.

For a suspected chemical burn, our first-aid reference says:
- Call 999 for medical help immediately. Do not wait for blistering or severe pain.
- Protect yourself with gloves. Carefully remove contaminated clothing if possible.
- Rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about one hour. Follow the call handler’s instructions.
- Do not use shampoo, creams, aloe or other chemicals, or try to neutralise it.
- Chemical burns need hospital assessment.

Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also mean 999 immediately.

Once help is underway, record what happened in the incident book: product, batch, mix, timings, symptoms and action taken. Keep dated notes and, with the client’s consent, photos. Keep client details private.

RETURNS — AND KEEPING EVIDENCE

The rep is in Tuesday, so affected bottles can go back to him, or to Kelvin Trade’s Hillington depot, for full credit.

BUT if you have had a problem with a bottle, keep that bottle back as evidence, with any remaining contents. Keep it sealed, clearly marked and safely out of use. Dinnae bin it, empty it or hand it back with routine returns before checking with your insurer about preserving evidence. Keep the supplier email and purchase details too.

Please make sure the other renters see this before mixing anything.

Kirsty
